candidates.issueBody: ### Describe the bug After upgrading to Next.js 16.0.10 (React2Shell CVE patch), the Radix UI `Slot` component silently fails to merge props onto child elements when used across a Server Component → Client Component boundary **in local development mode**. When using `asChild={true}` on a Client Component (e.g., Button with `"use client"`) inside a Server Component, the Slot's className and other props are not serialized/merged onto the child element. **The component silently doesn't render at all** - no errors in the console, no hydration warnings, nothing. This makes it extremely difficult to debug. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a Server Component (no `"use client"`) 2. Inside it, render a Client Component that uses Radix `Slot` with `asChild={true}` 3. Pass className to the component expecting Slot to merge it onto the child 4. Run `next dev` (local development mode) 5. The **entire component fails to render** with no error messages ``` // Server Component (card.tsx - no "use client") // Client Component (button/index.tsx - has "use client") const Comp = asChild ? Slot : "button"; return {children}### Expected behavior The `Slot` component should merge the className onto the child `` element, or at minimum throw an error/warning if serialization fails. ``` ### Actual behavior - The component silently doesn't render - No console errors or warnings - No React hydration mismatch warnings - `document.querySelector()` returns `null` for the element - Only discoverable by manually inspecting the DOM ### Workaround Moving the className directly onto the child element bypasses the issue: ### Environment - Next.js: 16.0.10 - React: 19.1.2 - @radix-ui/react-slot: 1.1.2 - Node: [your version] - OS: macOS ### Additional context - This regression appeared after updating to Next.js 16.0.10 which includes patches for CVE-2025-55182 (React2Shell) - The security patch likely changed RSC serialization behavior in a way that breaks Slot's prop merging across the RSC boundary - **The silent failure makes this extremely difficult to debug** - we spent significant time investigating caching issues, experiment systems, and other potential causes before discovering it was related to `asChild` - Removing `asChild` (rendering as `

comments.body:
This looks like the same root cause as #3776 — Slot doesn't handle RSC-serialized lazy references properly. I have a fix in #3777 that uses `Children.toArray` to resolve lazy children before `cloneElement`. This approach was validated by Mantine in [mantinedev/mantine#8522](https://github.com/mantinedev/mantine/pull/8522).

Would be great to get a maintainer review on #3777 — it's been open since December.

I think I'm having the same issue, and as of upgrading to Next.js v16.2.0 with Turbopack I get a runtime hydration error:

```
//    '+'   indicates it was rendered on client only

<Primitive.button type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded={false} ...>
  <Primitive.button.Slot type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded={false} ...>
    <Primitive.button.SlotClone type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded={false} ...>
+     <button
+       className="w-full text-center focus-visible:outline-none lg:w-64 lg:pl-5 lg:text-left"
+       type="button"
+       aria-haspopup="dialog"
+       aria-expanded={false}
+       aria-controls="radix-_R_5l5etqlb_"
+       data-state="closed"
+       onClick={function handleEvent}
+       ref={function}
+     >
```
Is this fixed by `@radix-ui/react-slot@1.2.4`? See https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/issues/3836.

comments.body: MAT-1767

Hey @kimballa thanks for opening the issue, and sorry about the outcome.

As we worked on that fix, we actually added a guard against breaking changes for users that would expect their Autocomplete to still behave as before without fullWidth passed. Essentially, passing the fullWidth prop as true to the Input if there's no fullWidth prop passed to the Autocomplete.

However, we did not guard against your use case. Since you are passing {false} and the 100% width from sx landing on the component root instead of the input, it is the expected outcome, after all. Unfortunately, it was discovered through a patch release that was not meant to break usages.

Please consider changing the usages of the component to make it take the whole space, in your example removing both fullWidth (or passing it as true to signal intention) and the sx should do. I'm sorry again for this unintentional side effect.

Thanks @silviuaavram . I appreciate the follow-up. I was able to work around things on my end. 

For what it's worth, my setup using the Autocomplete component is a _bit_ convoluted in that it's wrapped in a couple of layers of application-specific components (although many apps likely wrap MUI controls in more-complex application-specific component libraries). In any case, the `fullWidth` prop isn't actually passed in via direct prop-drilling; based on some other props, I render the component with `<Autocomplete .... fullWidth={otherProp === anotherCondition} sx={someStyleThings}>` so until this happened, I was always passing `fullWidth` explicitly one way or the other. 

I sort of understand what you're doing, but I _do_ think it's somewhat unique JSX API expectations that now `true`, `false`, and `undefined` actually have three distinct outcomes in how Autocomplete treats the prop. Boolean-typed props usually treat all false-ish values the same. If it's really not an "Autocomplete-wide" prop but is instead something you're forwarding to an internal component, that feels more like something that other MUI components put into nested `slotProps` maps that make their prop-drilled behavior explicit/visible to the caller (e.g., the `inputProps` map on the `<Select>` component).

At the very least I believe it deserves some very explicit documentation, as now it no longer behaves exactly like the `fullWidth` property used in several other components.  (Assuming your feedback implies the behavior I demonstrate is `not-a-bug`, this issue should probably turn into a documentation bug issue, as the [v7.3.8 API docs on your site](https://mui.com/material-ui/api/autocomplete/) states:

> If `true`, the input will take up the full width of its container.

... and lists the default value as `false`, which is now incorrect -- since otherwise my passing `false` in explicitly would have no effect. (It should probably list the default as `undefined` and include a note on how `undefined` and `false` are treated distinctly.)
That makes sense. I propose we update our API to make it clear that the fullWidth behaviour in Autocomplete is different, and give the reasoning for it. How's that sound, @kimballa ?

**This issue has been closed.** If you have a similar problem but not exactly the same, please open a [new issue](https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/new/choose).
Now, if you have additional information related to this issue or things that could help future readers, feel free to leave a comment.

---

@kimballa Thanks again for creating this issue! If you have a moment, we would love to hear your thoughts on how we handled it with this short [feedback form](https://tally.mui.com/support-satisfaction-survey?issue=47811&productId=material-ui).

## Problem

We are looking to move off using **Screener** as our Visual Regression testing solution for the entire monorepo by the end of the year.

## Solution
**Near Term**
- Near term plan is to integrate and use an internal **1JS VR** tool to replace screener for **v0, v7, v8, and v9**. The intent is for v0, v7 and v8 to stay with this solution going forward since they are legacy libraries.
	- [x] Integrate pipeline jobs to run 1JS VR tool (v9) #25606
		- [x] Only run VR test when package is affected #25676
	- [x] Integrate pipeline jobs to run 1JS VR tool (v8) #25643
		- [x] Only run VR test when package is affected #25676
	- [x] Add v0 stories to be used by 1JS VR tool #25663
	- [x] Integrate pipeline jobs to run 1JS VR tool (v0) #25922
	- [x] Intergrate pipeline jobs to run 1JS VR tool (v7) #25946
	- [x] Remove Screener workflow files (master branch) #25977
	- [x] Remove Screener pipeline job (v7 branch) #25990
	- [x] Replace any `Screener` imports with `StoryWright` for v8 #25979
	- [x] Replace any `Screener` imports with `StoryWright` for v9 #25980
	- [x] Replace any `Screener` imports with `StoryWright` for v7 #26049
	- [x] Remove any `Screener` related files from v0 #26053
	- [x] Remove `Screener` dependencies from package.json #26070
	- [x] Cleanup new 1JS VR tool yaml files (remove convert scripts,etc) #26070
	- [ ] Update any VR tool related docs in repo
	- [x] Delete `Screener` related github secrets #26086

**Long Term**
- Long term plan is to migrate **v9** VR tests to use **Chromatic** (Internal [Doc](https://microsoft-my.sharepoint-df.com/:w:/p/twatanabe/ETJng-7UQw9ClI4NDzfKFrcBO6miFceu_fxKhQx_Hy_6hw?e=ffgJ4o) writeup). This will have to be done in multiple steps: 
   - [x] Make `react-storybook-addon` configurable to be used by vr stories: #25162 
   - [ ] Refactor all v9 VR tests to use storybook Component Story Format (CSF)
   		- [x] Accordion #25525
   		- [x] Button #25108
   		- [x] Card #25526
   		- [x] Dialog #25527
   		- [x] Image #25527
   - [ ] Integrate Chromatic project for v9 into repo and make available for use
   - [ ] Slowly migrate each v9 component VR test to chromatic and refactor Screener interaction and hover tests to appropriate CSF equivalent. 
   - [ ] Colocate VR stories to their respective packages (i.e. move Menu VR tests to the `react-menu` package etc.)

<!-- Please provide all of the information requested below. We're a small team and without all of this information it's not possible for us to help and your bug report will be closed. -->

**What package within Headless UI are you using?**

@headlessui/vue

**What version of that package are you using?**

1.6.5

**What browser are you using?**

Chrome

**Reproduction URL**

https://headlessui.dev/vue/dialog

**Describe your issue**

No transitions take place when dialog initially appears or after closing/opening it again. Transition on close seems to work though. It used to work in v1.6.4.

comments.body: This is appears to be whenever there is a focussable (input/button) element within the dialog panel. The lack of transition used to occur on initial load of the component but now it appears to never transition when showing the panel.
Seems to be working in Safari, but not in Firefox or Chrome anymore... if that helps.
I'm seeing this too. Only when I have an input with autofocus turned on though.

Must have been introduced in `1.6.5`. Tested it in `1.6.4` with no problems. I see this issue on modals and slideovers, if the _first_ autofocussed item is an input. If it's a button the problem does not appear.

Problem appears on safari in my case, tool

Yeah, also happens in Safari.  https://headlessui.dev/vue/popover

The react version works fine though.

Can confirm that the issue is in `1.6.5`. Modals and slide-overs both skip their entrance transition classes and insta-render.

Safari did not have the issue in my use cases. Chrome and Firefox had it - in a Vite/Vue setup, a Vite/Vue/Ts setup, and a Nuxt 3 setup.

Downgrading to `1.6.4` solved the issue across all three implementations. 

And for what it's worth in my use cases, there were no inputs or anything. I had a slide-over and a dialog from the headlessUI site both balking on the animate in on the two browsers. No inputs involved. Just an icon close button or the default buttons from the headless examps.

I'm experiencing similar issues on react with v1.50, v1.6.4 and v1.6.5.

Reproduction URL: https://codesandbox.io/embed/tailwind-css-and-react-forked-wsiu2h

I'm experiencing the same problem. I had the v1.4.1 and decided to update to v.1.6.5 today and then I had this issue with the Transition component. I had to downgrade to v.1.50 in order to see this problem disappear. I'm going to skip v1.6+ for now.
same here

I have this same issue but with a variation that may provide clues as to the cause. Crucially, for me it (the "insta render/insta open bug) occurs **ONLY IN SPECIFIC CIRCUMSTANCES** in _1.6.4_, but **always** in 1.6.5. However, because I was able to reproduce the insta-open behavior under a specific circumstance in 1.6.4, I thought this could be useful to report in terms of tracking down the cause.

In the attached video, note that the slide-open transition appears properly when triggering (via a simple update of a `ref` reactive boolean which is tied to a prop of the slideover panel) from:
 - A regular button (button tag; not SFC)
 - A regular button as part of a button group (as a separate SFC)

However, note that when it is triggered from an open menu (Button group, with dropdown: https://tailwindui.com/components/application-ui/elements/button-groups), it instantly renders without transition.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5987153/176961871-5b394c62-8f02-4bce-9bc5-556edb59c96d.mp4


Given this, I am wondering if there is a (Headless UI internal) interaction between whatever's tracking the "open" state for both the Button group with dropdown, and the slideover?

On the other hand, I was not able to reproduce the issue with a minimal example, even using 1.6.4:

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-gdgttl-kvccnl?file=src/App.vue


My local project (as pictured in video; with hybrid behavior) versions:
Vue 3.2.25
@headlessui/vue 1.6.4
 Slideover and Button with dropdown components directly from TailwindUI with modification to pass props in, emit events out, etc.
I'm experiencing the same issue with @headlessui/vue 1.6.5, the initial animations won't work. For now downgrading to the previous version (1.6.4) fix the problem.

Same: @headlessui/vue 1.6.5.
If there is no focusable element works fine. The demo on the site is with the same issue.

Confirm, too only enter position are not working with `@headlessui/vue@1.6.5`

The example are not working either when choosing Vue (it works when you chose react)

I've been thinking I've been going crazy (maybe I missed something) the last week, and just gave up... until I tried a new popover and still no transition. Both glad and frustrated it's not just me. Gonna try the downgrade.

Seems to be related to focus-trap refactories since v1.5.0 - sadly Combobox "tab+focus" was broken in 1.5.0. So I had to find a workaround for any 1.6.x version, which is to pin to version 1.6.4 + handling `focus()` in dialogs by app logic.

This is all vue... btw.

Setup modals, panels with new `DialogPanel` (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/headlessui/releases/tag/%40headlessui%2Fvue%40v1.6.0)

now transitions work, but focus-trap is messed up (tab cycles through all other focusable elements first until stepping into modal, from now on stays in the trap). 

A fix is to force `focus()` onModalOpen by yourself, so let focus step into the trap.

Add event handler to TransitionRoot, ie.:
```vue
<TransitionRoot as="template" :show="isOpen" @after-enter="onEntered">
```

And with (template):

```html
<button ref="CancelButtonRef" type="button">
  Cancel
</button>
```

plus (script setup):

```js
const okButtonRef = ref(null)
```

candidates.issueBody:
**Describe the bug**

Rendering performance of Menu component (and possibly some others) got a lot worse (~8-10 times) after migrating a codebase to V1.0.

Description of a JSX layout rendered:
- 20 Boxes each having a Menu with 6 MenuItems

**Expected Behavior** 

Rendering of such a layout should be reasonably fast.

**Link to minimal reproduction** 

### V1.0 (huge lag when rendering):
~~https://codesandbox.io/s/staging-tree-fywty?file=/src/App.js~~
Updated Sandbox: https://codesandbox.io/s/inspiring-nightingale-wmmjs?file=/src/App.js

### Pre-V1.0, rendering is instant:
https://codesandbox.io/s/condescending-hugle-40nim?file=/src/App.js

**Steps to Reproduce** 

Open Sandbox, click on "Toggle" button to hide and then un-hide the thumbnails. Notice a significant lag while rendering the layout.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: OS X most recent
- Browser: Chrome
- Version: most recent

**Additional info**

React profiler screenshots - before V1.0:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/948486/86486971-b9f29d00-bd11-11ea-98fb-ad54a856e3ed.png)

React profiler screenshots - after V1.0 migration:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/948486/86486979-bc54f700-bd11-11ea-8f9a-51c5dae17260.png)

comments.body:
I am not sure if it is related or not, but I also saw pretty bad frame rate drops too while I scroll. But for me, I think I traced it back to Popper which I believe is used for `Menu`.  
  
You can actually just see the frame rate drops if you use https://next.chakra-ui.com/docs/components/menu and compare it to say for example https://next.chakra-ui.com/docs/components/modal. Simply scrolling causes the frame rate drops, no other interactions at all.

Menu example:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33623601/86489141-aa03a900-bd63-11ea-9e6c-9af9ffdf61ce.png)  
  
Modal example:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33623601/86489154-bab41f00-bd63-11ea-9ba2-bf07b17fb56e.png)

In my own project, I have the following. Which, if I comment out the use of `Menu` then I get a constant FPS.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33623601/86489322-4f1e8180-bd64-11ea-951f-1d97942af7d4.png)

We could add some tests for render times using a combination of [react-testing-library](https://github.com/testing-library/react-testing-library) and react [profiler api](https://reactjs.org/docs/profiler.html)

The `<Popover />` component seems to have the same behaviour: rendering although not visible through the [hidden](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/master/packages/popover/src/use-popover.ts#L176) attribute (just like `<Menu />` does [here](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/master/packages/menu/src/use-menu.ts#L395)).

Thanks for reporting this @dmitru. I spotted a couple of performance issues related to the styling API which is related to this and I've fixed this.

We can set up the Profiler API to measure the performance metrics and further improve the code. If it's related to popper, we need to confirm for sure.

As regards the rendering, we updated the "popover" components to render and stay hidden in the DOM to better collect the `refs` and `index` of each item in the tree, to improve keyboard navigation and handle nested menu scenarios.

In v0, we use `querySelector` to get these `refs` but we ran into some issues with nested menus and popovers hence the change.

We need to look into this some more but I believe the changes I've made will help a bit.

@segunadebayo Tried it by running a local repo clone (but not sure if I set it up correctly, there were some theming issues). I did not notice performance improvements – rendering a dozen of Menus still blocked the main thread for ~600ms. I'll give it another try as soon as the fixes are published (btw, I'd appreciate docs on how to install a Chakra clone locally in an existing project that used chakra from npm registry!)

The version I tested was: 7c0a7ebee6ea032a53eb78c1141f54416903517d

In my experience, the current approach to always rendering content for popovers and menus won't work performance-wise in some cases (I encounter them very often for the types of apps I'm building - think interactive graphical editors with sliders, color pickers and such). 

For example, in the app I'm building, there are some rendering-heavy components rendered inside Popovers, which are connected to a store (I'm using Mobx), and are re-rendered every time values change there... But I really only expect one Popover to be visible at any time (and then the performance is fine). Rendering all of their content just won't fly for me.

**As a suggestion**, perhaps we could have a `isLazy` prop or similar, for both Menus and Popovers, to defer rendering of content until these components open?

@segunadebayo **Update** The profiler shows a shallower render tree (which is good, great job on this one!), and also confirms that performance did improve slightly (but below the perception threshold).

(The version I tested was: 7c0a7ebee6ea032a53eb78c1141f54416903517d)
 
So far the improvemens for my case are (22ms to ~19ms) for one rendered Menu. 

Imagine how much better it'd be if Menu skipped rendering its children - it'd be down to 3ms! And the gains would be much more evident for longer / more complex content.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/948486/86930969-6e166e00-c0ec-11ea-8227-8fe2fa2d2b91.png)

Here's an updated Sandbox that illustrates the suggestion. Notice how rendering of the layout takes so much less time.  

Skipping rendering of Menu content allowed to bring the performance to an acceptable level:
https://codesandbox.io/s/blissful-mayer-g8vmu?file=/src/App.js

Still, there's a noticeable lag after a click on "Toggle thumbnails rendering" button, something I wouldn't expect from such a simple layout.

Comparison with a few other a11y-first libraries:

**Performance is ranked from best to worst.**
1. Chakra with skipped rendering of MenuItem's: https://codesandbox.io/s/blissful-mayer-g8vmu?file=/src/App.js
2. Reach: https://codesandbox.io/s/stoic-diffie-8zi65-reach-84b95?file=/src/App.js
3. Chakra without skipped rendering (default behavior): https://codesandbox.io/s/inspiring-nightingale-wmmjs?file=/src/App.js
4. Reakit is the slowest: https://codesandbox.io/s/stoic-diffie-8zi65-reakit-8zi65

It confirms that skipping rendering of MenuItems is the biggest possible performance gain.
@dmitru This is such thorough investigation! Thanks so much for the time and effort you're putting into this.

Thanks to @dmitru, we've implemented a solution for this.

Cheers guys

Hi @segunadebayo, 

I'm seem to be experiencing similar Menu performance issues with chakra-ui/core v1.0.0-rc.3. 

Could you confirm which which version has the solution implemented? And where in the code base the fix exists?

Thanks 👍

@jackhkmatthews could you please provide a codesandbox? You may simply add the `isLazy` prop to the `Menu` component to not render the `MenuList` contents until opened. Also you may upgrade to `rc.5`. For this kind of question, I'd recommend joining [our Discord](https://discord.gg/8nzYM2) as they can be easily resolved there.

[code](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/develop/packages/menu/src/use-menu.ts#L291)

@ljosberinn thanks for the quick response, code link and advice!

I'll be sure to join the discord and post there or here with any further questions

candidates.issueBody:
Operating system and version (Windows, macOS, Android, iOS)
- Windows 10, Build 19042 (10.0.19042)

Browser and version (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Microsoft Edge, Opera, Android Browser)
- Google Chrome, Version 87.0.4280.88 (Official Build) (64-bit)

--

_Note: This bug seems to have been introduced [during the transition](https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/commit/adfdf7160b5822aae12eea677e7dd3128d2569bf) from `"popper.js": "^1.16.1"` to `"@popperjs/core": "^2.5.4"`._

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Visit https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.5/components/popovers/#four-directions
2. Trigger "Popover on Left" and "Popover on Right"
3. Notice both adjust their position to be fully visible inside the body when viewport is sufficiently narrow
4. Visit https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.0/components/popovers/#four-directions
5. Trigger "Popover on Left" and "Popover on Right"
6. Notice both overflow the body when viewport is sufficiently narrow

![456](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1605754/101505935-79d7bc00-393a-11eb-97e8-11a6b4ba92d9.png)

### What is the expected behavior?

Expected behavior is for popovers to not overflow their container (like in Bootstrap 4.5.1).

### What went wrong?

It seems like there's been some change in the inline styles that are applied by Popper where we no longer perform:
`transform: translate3d(x, y, z)` 
and instead use:
`transform: translate(x, y)`.

![123](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1605754/101506119-ac81b480-393a-11eb-9643-7374e442dbb0.png)

### Any other comments?

Maybe [this change](https://github.com/popperjs/popper-core/blame/671f71e2b6990765e5ca780daaea7d1f7175beb6/src/modifiers/computeStyles.js#L106) from 10 months ago had something to do with it.

comments.body: It seems we got to explicitly define our fallback behaviour. See this demo, based on [popper's tutorial](https://popper.js.org/docs/v2/tutorial/): https://codepen.io/MartijnCuppens/pen/QWKKmLg?editors=1010 (Uncomment js for fix)
That was fast, thanks everyone!

2. Adjust viewport height with mouse or keyboard
3. Adjust library version with <kbd>↓</kbd>/<kbd>↑</kbd> keys

---

Here is a video capture that plays right on GitHub! Just click/tap on it 👇🏻
<video src=https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/27027/185394555-e7a59f5b-e7cf-4e41-85d4-f52a4ff7af7b.mp4 autoplay muted></video>

Temporarily worked around with `<sl-popup>.autoSize = false` because all of my `<sl-dropdown>`s are contained in the header which makes it possible use a single rule (`sl-dropdown::part(panel) { max-height: ⋯ }`) with a trivial calculation.

I have to say all this is really only possible and easy because of how well-designed [Shoelace](https://shoelace.style/) is! It truly is a gem of a library that shines bright among many that don't even grasp the power of web components, yet alone know what to do with the tech. 👟💎💖!

---

Still looking forward to a solution on this one that works for everyone though : )

Replicated and fixed in 1996037. The `auto-size` attribute was resizing both horizontally and vertically. This is now configurable in `<sl-popup>` and set to `vertical` in `<sl-dropdown>`, which restores the previous and desired behavior.

Hey,

I noticed that after #4879, an `EuiComboBox` with `singleSelection` will no longer scroll to the selected option on open.
You can verify this behavior by going to the [sandbox](https://codesandbox.io/s/eui-issue-ulk5f?file=/index.js) found in #4072, and alternating between versions 34.4.0 and 34.5.0. (open the first combobox in the sandbox)

I think this is because of line 158 added in `componentDidUpdate`, as this condition will never be true on mount.

https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/efad82b13106474c83f19eeb535e037b5af13e44/src/components/combo_box/combo_box_options_list/combo_box_options_list.tsx#L155-L161

I haven't sat down to think of a solution yet, maybe we could add a similar `scrollToItem` call in `componentDidMount`? (without this condition)
